content:
Dev Patel: Heads up — enterprise customer (Private deploy) is asking for a “stable runtime line” / LTS track as part of renewal. They’re basically saying “we can’t keep taking minor upgrades every few weeks just to get a fix.”

They want:
- predictable patch cadence (monthly-ish)
- clear backport rules (security/correctness/perf regressions)
- release notes that are ops-friendly (risk level, known issues)
- ability to pin in Private installer and rollback cleanly

Do we have something we can point them to that’s not vapor? I can pull in Product/Release Eng on the thread if we have dates.

Owen Phillips: Is this the same account from SUP-3921? (The one with the “change window once per quarter” constraint?)

Dev Patel: Yup, same org. They referenced the SUP ticket and basically said “we need an LTS channel like our other infra vendors provide.”

Marissa Cole: +1 they also asked last quarter for “risk tags” in release notes. They forwarded a screenshot of our current runtime notes and called them “too noisy.”

Dev Patel: Exactly. They asked “what changed and why should I care” not 50 internal refactor bullets.

Vivek Kulkarni: Looping in. For Private, we’re aligning installer semantics w/ the LTS versioning (pin + pull artifacts). It’s in flight but not GA yet.

Connor O'Brien: Release Eng here. We *do* have a real plan + drafts.
- PRD draft: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/PROD/Enterprise+Runtime+LTS+PRD
- Working dates (subject to final signoff):
  - branch cut pilot for `runtime-1.20-lts` targeting early Feb
  - first patch release `runtime-1.20-lts.0` shortly after (mid Feb-ish)
  - then monthly patch cadence unless there’s a security/urgent correctness fix

Guarantees we’re planning to offer:
- “slower change” = bug fixes, security fixes, narrowly scoped perf/stability fixes only
- no feature work / no large refactors backported
- explicit backport policy + required test evidence

I’d prefer we phrase dates as “pilot target weeks” until Mateo/SRE give final go/no-go.

Talia Benson: +1 on wording. We can share the direction + pilot timeline without committing to an SLA before the internal launch.

Suggested customer-safe language:
- LTS channel is launching as a pilot for select enterprise customers
- target first branch cut: week of Feb 3 (±1 week)
- support window details + backport rules will be published alongside first LTS patch notes

Also if they need something immediate, we can propose “pin to runtime 1.20.x on standard train + get a targeted hotfix backport” as interim.

Naomi Feldman: Please be careful on anything that reads like “12 months support” unless we have it approved. Some customers interpret that as contractual support duration.

We *can* say: “LTS will have a defined support window (published) and a predictable patch cadence” without giving the number yet.

Elliot Price: For comms: we have a release notes template draft that’s much more ops-focused (risk level, behavior changes, mitigations, upgrade steps). I can share a screenshot / excerpt if that helps the customer feel it’s real.

Connor O'Brien: Also, if they’re asking “what’s different from normal releases”:
- LTS will have additional CI gates + artifact provenance/signing checks
- perf regression gates (p95/p99 thresholds) and canary requirements before we promote patches

Those are in the eng docs drafts, but PRD is the best customer-facing thing right now.

Dev Patel: This is super helpful. For the customer reply, can I say:
1) we’re piloting a `runtime-1.20-lts` line for Private/Dedicated enterprise
2) target branch cut early Feb; first patch mid Feb; monthly cadence
3) backports limited to security/correctness/stability/perf regressions w/ strict test gates
4) release notes will include risk levels + known issues + mitigations

…and include the PRD link?

Naomi Feldman: Yes to (1)-(4), but I’d soften (2) to “targeting early Feb / mid Feb” and avoid “monthly” as a promise; “regular cadence (typically monthly)” is safer.

Connor O'Brien: Agree. Also, PRD link is fine if they’re OK with “draft / subject to change” status. If you want, I can DM you a shorter blurb that’s customer-ready.

Vivek Kulkarni: Add a line that Private installer support for pinning LTS artifacts is part of the pilot scope. They’ve asked explicitly for this.

Dev Patel: Got it. I’ll respond with the softened dates + mention installer pinning/rollback guidance is included.

Can someone confirm who owns the “select customers” list? They asked if they can be in the pilot.

Talia Benson: I’m coordinating the pilot cohort list w/ Product + Release Eng. For now tell them: “We’re selecting a small set of enterprise Private customers for the pilot; we can nominate your account and confirm after internal readiness review.”

Owen Phillips: Perfect. Also, do we have an internal ticket I should reference when Support gets more of these asks?

Connor O'Brien: There’s a Linear epic “Runtime LTS branch & release process” (ENG-4821). For Support tracking, keep using SUP tickets + link the PRD. We’ll share an internal FAQ once #announcements goes out.

Dev Patel: Thanks all. I’ll draft the customer email now and loop in if they push for hard commitments.
